data.one_liner: Dartlang port of socket.io-client for web, flutter, and dartvm
data.what_it_does: Provides a client implementation to connect to Socket.io servers from Dart and Flutter applications. Supports web, Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms using WebSockets.
use_when: You need real-time, bidirectional event-based communication with a Socket.io backend.
Building cross-platform Flutter or pure Dart applications that require WebSocket connectivity with Socket.io.
avoid_when: You are using simple REST endpoints where standard HTTP requests are sufficient.
Your backend does not use the Socket.io protocol.
strengths: Supports reconnection logic, custom headers, and explicit transport settings.
Compatible across web, desktop, and mobile Flutter environments.
weaknesses: Socket instances are cached by scheme, port, and host, requiring careful handling of configuration options on initial creation.
Extra headers cannot be sent on the WebSocket handshake on web browsers.
data.setup_notes: On macOS, ensure network client entitlements are configured. On Android/iOS, check network security policies for HTTP connections if not using HTTPS.
